Late-Han Chinese dress — cross-collared silk robes with wide sleeves and a broad sash, lamellar or scale armor laced with cords where armor is worn, bronze, jade and lacquer ornament, Han court hair ornaments; silk, lacquered leather, bronze and iron.

Colours: crimson red, gold, river teal, black lacquer.
Signature item: a chancellery seal. She holds it at full scale: one whole object, drawn once, held in front of or beside her body; a long weapon keeps one straight, unbroken shaft with a single head or blade.
Exposure (bold): her robes open to show skin — the cross collar opened into a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare upper arms above detached wide sleeves (and bare shoulders where no shoulder guard sits), the skirt panels cut with a high side slit at full length — it shows the side line of one leg as she stands, no leg pushed out or knee bent for it; any armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: a soft key light with a strong rim light tracing her hair, shoulders and armour; bright, crisp specular highlights on metal and jewellery, and a clean, warm-neutral sheen on her skin.
Composition: her whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet inside the frame with clear margins, about four-fifths of the image height; camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective.

One figure only — no second character, horse or other creature. No readable text or numbers, except that a banner, seal or emblem may carry the single character 吳 or 顧. No logo, watermark, speech bubble or frame border. Three Kingdoms-era Chinese dress, architecture and materials only.
Avoid: a blue or bruise-like tint on the skin around the eyes, glossy or shiny highlights on the face, sweaty, oily or plastic-looking skin.
